title: Frobenius Number for Three or More Generators: Monotonicity and the Sylvester Upper Bound
description: For three or more generators the Frobenius number has no closed form (the problem is NP-hard), so the honest target is a bound. This entry proves the structural fact missing from Mathlib: the Frobenius number is monotone (antitone) in the generating set — adding generators can only make more numbers representable, hence only lowers the largest non-representable number. Consequence: any generating set containing a coprime pair m, n > 1 has a Frobenius number g ≤ m·n − m − n (Sylvester's two-generator value), giving the explicit three-generator bound g(m, n, k) ≤ m·n − m − n. A strictness theorem shows the bound drops strictly whenever the old boundary value becomes representable. 6 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms; builds on Mathlib's frobeniusNumber_pair and exists_frobeniusNumber_iff.

conclusion.summary: Building directly on Mathlib's `FrobeniusNumber` development, this entry supplies the structural result Mathlib lacks — **monotonicity of the Frobenius number in the generating set** — and derives from it a computable upper bound for the three-or-more-generator Frobenius number. The centrepiece `frobeniusNumber_antitone` states: if $s \subseteq t$ and both sets have Frobenius numbers $f, g$, then $g \le f$. Applied to a coprime pair $\{m, n\} \subseteq s$ and Sylvester's two-generator formula $g(m, n) = m n - m - n$ (Mathlib's `frobeniusNumber_pair`), this yields the main bound $g(s) \le m n - m - n$ for any generating set $s$ containing $m, n$. A strictness companion `frobeniusNumber_lt_of_mem_closure` shows $g(t) < g(s)$ exactly when the old Frobenius value of $s$ becomes representable in the larger $t$ — so the two-generator formula is a genuine (and typically non-tight) *upper* bound for three or more generators, matching the well-known fact that no closed form exists for $n \ge 3$. 6 theorems, 0 axioms, 0 sorries.
conclusion.implications: **The elementary bound for the general Frobenius problem, formally verified.** For $n \ge 3$ coprime generators the Frobenius number $g(a_1, \ldots, a_n)$ has no closed form — it is the subject of algorithms (Selmer, Brauer, the Beihoffer–Hendry–Nijenhuis–Wagon round-robin) and asymptotic bounds (Erdős–Graham, Kannan). The monotonicity bound proved here is the most elementary of all these: the two-generator Sylvester formula, applied to *any* coprime pair sitting inside the generating set, is a valid upper bound for the whole set. The strictness theorem quantifies the slack: the bound is exact only for the coprime pair itself and drops the moment any additional generator was previously a gap at the boundary. **Reusable infrastructure**: `frobeniusNumber_antitone` and `frobeniusNumber_lt_of_mem_closure` are stated for arbitrary sets and are candidates for upstreaming to Mathlib, which currently proves only the two-generator value and the existence criterion but nothing about how the invariant behaves under enlarging the generating set. **Numerical-semigroup reading**: monotonicity is the statement that the genus/Frobenius invariants are order-reversing along the inclusion lattice of numerical semigroups generated by finite sets — a lattice-theoretic fact underlying, e.g., the tree of numerical semigroups by genus.
openQuestions: **Sharper multi-generator bounds.** The monotonicity bound $g(a_1, \ldots, a_n) \le a_i a_j - a_i - a_j$ (best coprime pair) is rarely tight. Can the Erdős–Graham bound $g(a_1, \ldots, a_n) \le 2 a_{n} \lfloor a_1 / n \rfloor - a_1$ or the Selmer bound be formalized on top of this infrastructure, and how do they compare to the pairwise bound on concrete families?

**Exact three-generator value on structured families.** For arithmetic-progression generators $\{a, a+d, a+2d\}$ with $\gcd(a, d) = 1$, Roberts (1956) gives a closed form for the Frobenius number. Formalize this and check it against the monotonicity upper bound proved here.

**Lattice monotonicity to a genus statement.** Monotonicity of the Frobenius number established here is the ordinal shadow of a stronger cardinal fact: the *genus* (number of gaps) is also antitone in the generating set. Prove `genus t ≤ genus s` for `s ⊆ t` using Mathlib's `Nat.finite_setOf_setGcd_dvd_and_mem_span`, generalizing the two-generator genus formula of sibling OQ-01.

overview.historicalContext:
The **Frobenius coin problem** asks for the largest integer $g(a_1, \ldots, a_n)$ not representable as a nonnegative integer combination of given generators. **J. J. Sylvester** (1884) solved the two-generator case completely: for coprime $a, b > 1$, $g(a, b) = ab - a - b$ (the *Chicken McNugget theorem*). For **three or more generators the problem has no closed-form solution** — Frobenius himself popularized the general question in his lectures, and it is now known to be NP-hard (Ramírez Alfonsín, 1996). What *is* available for $n \ge 3$ are algorithms (Brauer 1942; Selmer 1977; Beihoffer–Hendry–Nijenhuis–Wagon 2005) and bounds (Erdős–Graham 1972; Kannan 1992).

This entry formalizes the **most elementary bound** of all, which follows from a single structural observation absent from Mathlib: the Frobenius number is **monotone (antitone) in the generating set**. Mathlib's `Mathlib.NumberTheory.FrobeniusNumber` (Alex Zhao, Daniel Buth, Sebastian Meier, Junyan Xu) proves the two-generator value `frobeniusNumber_pair` and the existence criterion `exists_frobeniusNumber_iff` (a Frobenius number exists iff the set-gcd is 1 and 1 is not a generator), but says nothing about how the invariant responds to adding generators. Supplying that monotonicity, and reading off the resulting upper bound for three or more generators, is the contribution here.
overview.problemStatement:
Let $s$ be a set of natural-number generators. Using Mathlib's definition $\mathrm{FrobeniusNumber}\,g\,s \iff g = \max\{k : k \notin \langle s\rangle_{\mathbb{N}}\}$ (largest non-representable element), prove:

1. **Monotonicity:** if $s \subseteq t$, $\mathrm{FrobeniusNumber}\,f\,s$ and $\mathrm{FrobeniusNumber}\,g\,t$, then $g \le f$.
2. **Strict decrease:** if in addition $f \in \langle t\rangle_{\mathbb{N}}$ (the old Frobenius value becomes representable), then $g < f$.
3. **Upper bound from a coprime pair:** if $m, n \in s$ are coprime with $m, n > 1$ and $1 \notin s$, then $s$ has a Frobenius number $g$ with $g \le mn - m - n$.
4. **Three generators:** for coprime $m, n > 1$ and any $k > 1$, $g(m, n, k) \le mn - m - n$, strictly when $k = mn - m - n$.
overview.text: The Frobenius number is antitone in the generating set — adding generators only lowers it — which turns Sylvester's two-generator formula into a formally verified upper bound for the open three-or-more-generator problem.
overview.proofStrategy: **Monotonicity `frobeniusNumber_antitone`** is three lines: `AddSubmonoid.closure_mono` gives $\langle s\rangle \le \langle t\rangle$; since the Frobenius number $g$ of $t$ is not in $\langle t\rangle$ it is not in $\langle s\rangle$ either; and $f$, being the *greatest* non-member of $\langle s\rangle$ (the `IsGreatest` half of Mathlib's definition), dominates it — `hf.2 hg_not_s`. **Strictness `frobeniusNumber_lt_of_mem_closure`** upgrades $g \le f$ to $g < f$ by ruling out equality: $g = f$ would force $f \notin \langle t\rangle$, contradicting the hypothesis $f \in \langle t\rangle$. **The bound `frobeniusNumber_le_pair`** combines existence and monotonicity: a coprime pair forces the set-gcd to be $1$ (`setGcd_eq_one_of_coprime`, via `Nat.setGcd_dvd_of_mem` + `Nat.dvd_gcd`), so `exists_frobeniusNumber_iff` yields a Frobenius number, and `frobeniusNumber_antitone` against `frobeniusNumber_pair` on $\{m, n\} \subseteq s$ gives the bound. **The three-generator corollaries** specialize $s = \{m, n, k\}$, discharging the membership and $1 \notin s$ side-goals by `simp`/`omega`.
keyInsights: **Monotonicity is the whole game.** Almost every other multi-generator bound reduces to the two-generator case plus the observation that extra generators only help. Mathlib had the two-generator formula but not this observation; once `frobeniusNumber_antitone` is available, the upper bound for arbitrarily many generators is a one-line corollary. The proof is a pure `IsGreatest` + `closure_mono` argument — no arithmetic.

**Honesty about `n ≥ 3`: a bound, not a formula.** No closed form exists for three or more generators (NP-hard in general), so claiming an exact value would be false. The entry deliberately proves an *upper bound* and, via `frobeniusNumber_lt_of_mem_closure`, exhibits when it is strict — matching the true mathematical status of the open problem.

**Existence rides on the coprime pair.** A single coprime pair $m, n \in s$ forces $\gcd(s) = 1$ because $\gcd(s) \mid m$ and $\gcd(s) \mid n$, hence $\gcd(s) \mid \gcd(m, n) = 1$. Combined with $1 \notin s$, Mathlib's `exists_frobeniusNumber_iff` then guarantees the Frobenius number of the whole set exists — so the bound is not vacuous.

**Strictness is a boundary phenomenon.** The bound $g(m, n, k) \le mn - m - n$ becomes strict precisely when the added generator $k$ makes the old maximal gap $mn - m - n$ representable — e.g. $k = mn - m - n$ itself. For $\{3, 5, 7\}$ the true value is $g = 4 < 7 = g(3, 5)$: the extra generator $7$ collapses the boundary gap.

**Reusable, upstreamable API.** `frobeniusNumber_antitone` and `frobeniusNumber_lt_of_mem_closure` are stated for arbitrary `Set ℕ`, independent of the coprime-pair application. They fill a genuine gap in `Mathlib.NumberTheory.FrobeniusNumber`, which characterizes existence and the two-generator value but not the behaviour of the invariant under set inclusion.
prerequisites: Mathlib `FrobeniusNumber g s := IsGreatest {k | k ∉ AddSubmonoid.closure s} g` (largest non-representable element)
Mathlib `frobeniusNumber_pair` : g(m, n) = m·n − m − n for coprime m, n > 1
Mathlib `exists_frobeniusNumber_iff` : a Frobenius number exists iff setGcd s = 1 and 1 ∉ s

crossReferences.description: Direct parent open question: OQ-01 asks to generalize the two-generator genus count to three or more generators. This entry answers the Frobenius-number half of that question with a monotonicity bound, and explicitly flags that no closed form exists for n ≥ 3.
The root Sylvester theorem g(a, b) = ab − a − b for two coprime generators. The monotonicity bound proved here applies that two-generator value to any coprime pair inside a larger generating set.

The three-generator representability companion (Representable3 a b c n). This entry provides the complementary upper bound on the three-generator Frobenius number that OQ-03's representability predicate leaves open.
Coprimality of a pair (gcd = 1) is exactly what makes the set-gcd 1 and forces the Frobenius number to exist; Bézout's identity is the arithmetic content of that coprimality hypothesis.

mathlibDependencies.description: Sylvester's two-generator value g(m,n) = m·n − m − n for coprime m, n > 1 — the quantity used as the upper bound
A Frobenius number exists iff the set-gcd is 1 and 1 is not a generator — used to guarantee the bound is non-vacuous
Monotonicity of additive-submonoid closure — the engine of the monotonicity proof
The gcd of a set of naturals divides each member — used to derive setGcd s = 1 from a coprime pair
A common divisor of m and n divides gcd(m, n) — combines the two divisibilities into setGcd s ∣ 1

originalContributions: frobeniusNumber_antitone: the Frobenius number is monotone (antitone) in the generating set — s ⊆ t ⟹ g(t) ≤ g(s); this structural fact is absent from Mathlib
frobeniusNumber_lt_of_mem_closure: strict decrease when the old Frobenius value becomes representable in the larger set — quantifies the slack in the bound
frobeniusNumber_le_pair: any generating set containing a coprime pair m, n > 1 has a Frobenius number ≤ m·n − m − n (existence + bound)
frobeniusNumber_triple_le: explicit three-generator upper bound g(m, n, k) ≤ m·n − m − n from a single coprime pair
frobeniusNumber_triple_strict: the three-generator bound is strict when the third generator equals the old boundary value m·n − m − n

openQuestions.question: Formalize the Erdős–Graham bound g(a_1,…,a_n) ≤ 2·a_n·⌊a_1/n⌋ − a_1 on top of this monotonicity infrastructure and compare it to the pairwise Sylvester bound on concrete generator families.
Prove the genus is also antitone in the generating set (genus t ≤ genus s for s ⊆ t), generalizing the two-generator genus formula of sibling OQ-01 via Mathlib's finiteness of the gap set.

sections.title: Module Header, Motivation, and Imports
sections.summary: Doc comment framing the three-or-more-generator Frobenius problem: no closed form exists (NP-hard), so the target is a monotonicity-based upper bound. Imports Mathlib.NumberTheory.FrobeniusNumber and Mathlib.Tactic; opens namespace FrobeniusMultiGenerator.
sections.mathContext: Mathlib supplies frobeniusNumber_pair (two-generator value) and exists_frobeniusNumber_iff (existence), but not monotonicity of the invariant under enlarging the generating set.

sections.title: Monotonicity of the Frobenius Number
sections.summary: frobeniusNumber_antitone: if s ⊆ t and both have Frobenius numbers f, g, then g ≤ f. Three-line proof via AddSubmonoid.closure_mono and the IsGreatest characterization.
sections.mathContext: The reusable, upstreamable core: the Frobenius invariant is antitone along the inclusion lattice of finitely generated submonoids of ℕ.

sections.title: Strict Decrease at the Boundary
sections.summary: frobeniusNumber_lt_of_mem_closure: if additionally the old Frobenius value f becomes representable in t, then g < f strictly. Upgrades g ≤ f by ruling out equality.
sections.mathContext: Quantifies the slack in the bound: any added generator that fills the old maximal gap forces a strict drop (e.g. {3,5,7} gives 4 < 7).

sections.title: A Coprime Pair Forces setGcd = 1
sections.summary: setGcd_eq_one_of_coprime: coprime m, n in s implies setGcd s = 1, via Nat.setGcd_dvd_of_mem and Nat.dvd_gcd. The existence hook for the bound.
sections.mathContext: A single coprime pair inside s collapses the set-gcd to 1, with no assumption on the other generators.

sections.title: Main Upper Bound from a Coprime Pair
sections.summary: frobeniusNumber_le_pair: any set s containing a coprime pair m, n > 1 with 1 not in s has a Frobenius number g at most m*n - m - n. Combines existence (exists_frobeniusNumber_iff) with monotonicity against frobeniusNumber_pair.
sections.mathContext: The elementary upper bound for the general Frobenius problem: Sylvester's two-generator value on any coprime pair inside the set.

sections.title: Explicit Three-Generator Bound and Strict Case
sections.summary: frobeniusNumber_triple_le: g(m, n, k) at most m*n - m - n for coprime m, n > 1 and any k > 1. frobeniusNumber_triple_strict: strict when k = m*n - m - n. Side-goals discharged by simp/omega.
sections.mathContext: Directly answers the three-or-more-generators open question with a computable, verified bound, honestly framed as an upper bound (no closed form exists for n >= 3).
